name: Row-aware Hadamard tightening of the full N=1 finite inverse radius

statement.note_ascii: on the already-certified full N=1 49-dimensional symmetry slice, retain one Jacobian-row and Hessian-row majorant per selected Taylor observation instead of replacing all rows by the largest row; integer nonzero determinant plus row-wise Hadamard cofactor bounds then give q<=1/2 at a much larger rigorous radius

definitions.J_0: integer-row-scaled selected 49x49 shell-energy Taylor-jet Jacobian at the small-integer N=1 center
definitions.R_j: finite certified l1 majorant for selected Jacobian row j at the center
definitions.H_j: finite certified Jacobian-row variation majorant per unit infinity-radius on the enclosing norm-4 box
definitions.C_j: row-aware cofactor bound product_{k != j} R_k
definitions.r: strictly positive finite state-space radius chosen so the preconditioned Jacobian defect is at most one half

parents.evidence: the 49-dimensional local inverse chart and nonzero integer-scaled determinant are already certified
replaces 49*Jmax^48*Hmax by the row-aware sum of cofactor and Hessian products while preserving the same q<=1/2 proof architecture
the rigorous radius improves by more than four thousand decimal orders but remains far below practical measurement scale, so the entrywise-preconditioned frontier remains open

claim_boundary: Finite N=1 tightening only. It improves a rigorous positive-radius lower bound, not the actual conditioning of the inverse. It is still based on conservative derivative majorants and determinant >=1, does not supply a practical sensor/noise tolerance, does not certify global branch uniqueness, does not extend automatically to arbitrary N, and has no continuum-regularity or Clay implication.
